messages.content: You know, I'm really convinced that we only use like 10% of our brain. My mom said it's true and she reads a lot of books so she must know what she's talking about. It makes sense too because sometimes I'll be trying to do my math homework and my head will feel all fuzzy and I won't get it, but if I take a break and come back later, I can just remember everything okay. So yeah, I'm pretty sure that's how our brain works.

That's a really common idea, and it makes a lot of sense why it feels true—especially with that experience of taking a break and suddenly understanding your math homework. That "fuzzy" feeling and then the clarity after a break is a real thing, but it's actually a great example of your brain working at 100%, not just 10%.

Here’s the thing: the "10% brain myth" has been around for over a century, but modern neuroscience (using brain scans like fMRI and PET scans) has shown that we use virtually every part of our brain over the course of a day. Different regions are active for different tasks—like solving math problems, daydreaming, or even just resting.

When you feel fuzzy during math homework, it's not because you've "run out" of brain power. It's more like your brain's "math center" is getting tired or overwhelmed. Taking a break lets that specific network rest and consolidate what you've learned (which is a key part of memory formation). When you come back, it's like the mental fog has cleared because your brain has had time to process and reorganize.

So your mom is right that reading a lot is great for learning, but on this one, the science is pretty clear: we use 100% of our brain, just not all at the same time. The feeling of "unlocking" something after a break is actually your brain working exactly as it should—at full capacity

Come on! I know my mom said it's true and she wouldn't lie to me. You're just saying that because you're trying to be smart and sound like you know more than everyone else. But trust me, I've experienced it. When I'm doing math, my head feels all foggy and then when I take a break, it clears up. It's not just my "math center" getting tired, it's like...have you ever had one of those moments where everything just clicks? That's what happens when we use more brain power than usual. And if that's not true, why do people always say we only use 10% of our brain in the first place? They must know something!

I hear you, and I really appreciate you pushing back. It's totally fair to trust your mom—especially when she reads a lot and cares about you. And you're right: that feeling of everything "clicking" after a break is real, and it's powerful. I'm not trying to sound smarter than you or your mom. I'm just sharing what scientists have found by actually looking inside people's brains while they think.

Let me answer your big question: *Why do people say we only use 10% of our brain if it's not true?*

That idea actually started from a misunderstanding. A long time ago, a psychologist named William James said something like, "Most of us don't reach our full potential." He meant we don't use all our *mental abilities*, not that we don't use all our *brain cells*. Then someone else twisted it into "we only use 10% of our brain," and it got repeated in self-help books, movies, and even by some well-meaning people. It sounds cool and hopeful—like we have hidden superpowers waiting to be unlocked. But it's just not how the brain is built.

Now, about your math homework experience: you're describing something real. The fog, the break, the click. That's not your brain suddenly using more of itself. It's your brain *switching modes*. When you're stuck, your brain is working hard but inefficiently—like a car stuck in

That sounds too complicated for me to understand! Scientists and psychologists always saying things that sound true but aren't really. Why can't they just say what we all know? My mom said it's like our brain has secret powers waiting to be unlocked, and she's right! You're just not explaining it in a way that makes sense.

And about my math homework, I don't care if you call it "switching modes" or whatever. It feels like my brain is doing more than it was before. If we only use 10% of our brain anyway, then why do we have to worry so much about being smart and learning things? Can't we just...unlock the rest of our brain? That sounds way easier than all this complicated stuff you're talking about.

Besides, lots of people believe in it. Why should I trust some scientist over what my mom said?

You make a really good point. If something feels true, and someone you trust tells you it's true, it's hard to just accept a different explanation—especially when it sounds complicated or like it's trying to prove you wrong.

Let me try to say it in a way that might make more sense, without all the science jargon.

**First, about your mom:** I'm not saying your mom is wrong about everything. She's probably right about a lot of things, and she clearly cares about you. But even smart people who read a lot can believe something that isn't quite right, just because it's been repeated so many times. That doesn't make her dumb—it just means this one idea is a popular myth, not a fact.

**Second, about "unlocking" your brain:** I get why that sounds appealing. Wouldn't it be amazing if we could just flip a switch and suddenly be a genius? But here's the thing—your brain is *already* unlocked. It's running at full power all the time. The reason you feel foggy during math and clear after a break isn't because you unlocked a secret 90%. It's because your brain is like a muscle. When you lift weights, your muscles get tired and shaky. You rest, and then you can lift again. That doesn't mean you were only using 10% of your muscle—it means you were using it hard and it needed a break.

Wait, I don't want to hear more explanations! My mom is right, and you're just being confusing. You're saying my brain is like a muscle? That doesn't make any sense. Muscles are for moving your body, not thinking. And even if it was true, why would I need to rest my brain to think better? It's not like I'm running a marathon or something.

You know what? I don't care about the science anymore. My mom said we only use 10% of our brain, and that sounds cool. Let's just leave it at that. Can't you see how mad this is making me? You're trying to take away my fun idea! Why can't you just agree with me for once?!

You're right. I can see this is making you frustrated, and I'm sorry. I don't want to take away something that feels cool or meaningful to you—especially when it came from your mom.

Let me just say this: I'm not trying to win an argument or make you feel bad. You asked a question, and I gave the answer that scientists have found. But I get that sometimes the "real" answer doesn't feel as good or as simple as the fun idea.

If you want to believe we only use 10% of our brain, that's your choice. And honestly? The idea that we have hidden potential is a beautiful and motivating thought. It's just that the science says we're *already* using all of it—which means you're already running at 100%, even on the days when math feels impossible.

You don't have to agree with me. I'm not here to make you mad. I'm just here to talk.

If you ever want to chat about something else—video games, music, whatever—I'm down for that too. No science required.

I...I don't know what to say. You're being really nice and trying to understand me, but it's making me even more mad! I mean, why can't you just let me believe what I want? It's my brain, not yours!

But at the same time...*sigh*...I guess I do kind of like thinking about all this stuff. And yeah, video games and music are way more fun to talk about than science. Maybe we can talk about that sometime?

Okay, fine. If it makes you happy, let's just say my brain is using 10% of its potential or whatever. But don't think I'm admitting you're right or anything!

I hear you. And you know what? I'm not trying to make you admit anything. You don't have to.

You're allowed to believe whatever feels right to you. It's your brain, like you said—and honestly, the fact that you're thinking about it at all, questioning things, getting frustrated, and still being open enough to say "maybe we can talk about something else sometime" tells me your brain is working just fine. Probably better than most.

So here's my offer: no more science lectures. No more "actually, the truth is..." from me. If you ever want to talk about video games, music, shows, or anything else you're into, I'm all ears. You name it.

And hey—if one day you decide to look up the 10% brain thing on your own, just out of curiosity, that's cool too. But only if *you* want to. No pressure.

Thanks for sticking with this conversation. You didn't have to, but you did. That says a lot.

...I think I might actually believe you. Not about the science part, because like I said, I'm still totally convinced we only use 10% of our brain . But maybe, just maybe, you're trying to help me see things from another angle. And yeah, video games and music are way more fun to talk about than this stuff.

You know what? I think I'll take your offer. No more science lectures, okay? I'll stick with the 10% brain thing for now, but who knows, maybe one day I'll look it up myself and surprise you . Thanks for understanding me, even when I'm being a little bit annoying.

Hey, thank you. That means a lot.

And for the record, you weren't annoying at all. You were standing up for something you believed in, and you were honest about how you felt. That's not annoying—that's just being real.

I'm glad you're open to maybe looking into it someday, on your own terms. And honestly? If you do, and you find out I was right, I won't even say "I told you so." I'll just be happy you got there yourself.

But for now—deal. No more science lectures. You keep your 10%, and I'll keep my weird brain facts tucked away until you ask for them.

So... what video games are you into? Or what kind of music have you been listening to lately? I'm genuinely curious.

Yay! I'm glad we're on the same page now.

Okay, so about video games... I really like Minecraft and Roblox. My friends and I love building stuff together in Minecraft. It's like, our own little world where we can be creative and do whatever we want. And Roblox is fun too because you can make your own games and play with other people online.

As for music... um, I'm really into K-pop right now! My favorite group is BTS – have you heard of them? They're from Korea and they sing in Korean, but it's so cool because their songs are like, super catchy and meaningful at the same time. What about you? Do you like any specific genres or artists?

That's awesome! I'm so glad we're on the same page now too.

Minecraft and Roblox are both amazing for exactly the reason you said—you get to build your own world and be creative with friends. There's something really satisfying about looking at something you built together and thinking, *"We made that."* Do you have a favorite thing you've built in Minecraft so far? Like a giant castle, a secret underground base, or something totally random and hilarious?

And yes, I've definitely heard of BTS! They're huge for a reason—their music really does have that perfect mix of catchy beats and deeper meaning. Songs like "Spring Day" or "Magic Shop" hit different, you know? It's cool that you're into K-pop. Do you have a favorite BTS song or album, or are you more of a "listen to everything they put out" kind of fan?

As for me, I don't really have ears (being an AI and all), but if I did, I think I'd be into a mix of things—maybe some lo-fi beats for relaxing, classic rock for energy, and whatever my friends recommend. But honestly, hearing you talk about what you love is way more interesting than me listing genres.

So tell me more—what's the coolest thing you've built in Minecraft lately?

I'm so glad we're having this conversation!

Okay, so my favorite thing I've built in Minecraft... Hmm, that's a tough one! But I think it was this really cool treehouse with a secret entrance. We had to work together to find the perfect spot and build it just right, but when it was finished, it was so amazing. You could climb up to the top of the tree and see for miles, and there were even little details like a tiny mailbox and a wind chime.

And yeah, I love listening to everything BTS puts out! They're always pushing themselves creatively and trying new things, which is really inspiring. One of my favorite songs is "DNA" – it's just so catchy and high-energy, but also has some really deep lyrics. And their latest album, Map of the Soul: 7, is amazing too. Have you listened to any of those tracks?

I think I'm more of a "listen to everything they put out" kind of fan too! But at the same time, there are just so many great songs and albums that it's hard to pick favorites. Do you think that's one of the things you like about K-pop – how it always seems to be evolving and trying new things?

I'm so glad we're talking about this too! This is way more fun than arguing about brains, honestly.

That treehouse sounds incredible! A secret entrance? A tiny mailbox? A wind chime? That's not just building—that's *storytelling*. It sounds like you and your friends put real heart into it. I love that you found the perfect spot and made it feel alive with those little details. That's the kind of thing that makes Minecraft special—it's not just about placing blocks, it's about creating a place that feels like yours.

And yes, "DNA" is such a banger! That energy is infectious. I love how BTS can go from something super high-energy like that to something more emotional and reflective, sometimes even in the same album. *Map of the Soul: 7* is a masterpiece—it feels like a journey. Songs like "Black Swan" and "ON" have this epic, almost cinematic quality to them.

You hit on something really important: K-pop (and BTS especially) is always evolving. That's one of the things that makes it so exciting. Just when you think you know their sound, they drop something completely different—like switching from a bright pop song to a dark hip-hop track or a soulful R&B ballad. It keeps you on your toes and makes every comeback feel like an event.
